legal_basis.value: Betäubungsmittelgesetz (BetmG, SR 812.121) Art. 8 Abs. 5 — BAG exceptional permits for limited medical use of prohibited narcotics

access_pathway_details.text: Under Art. 8(5) of the Narcotics Act (BetmG), the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) grants treating physicians case-by-case exceptional permits for limited medical use of LSD, MDMA or psilocybin in individual patients. Each permit covers one patient and one substance, is valid for one year and may be renewed; there is no entitlement to a permit.

eligibility_requirements.text: Serious illness where conventional treatments have been exhausted and relief can be expected. Anxiety disorders are among the most common primary indications. The physician's application includes the patient's written consent.

provider_requirements.text: Only the treating physician can apply to the BAG. Permit holders are usually specialists in psychiatry and psychotherapy; parts of the treatment can be delegated to other professionals.

oversight_notes.text: BAG per-patient exceptional permit system in place since 2014; about 1,800 permits (initial and renewals) were issued from 2014 to the end of 2024. It is an exception under narcotics law, not a marketing authorisation.

cost_notes.text: Billing within the Swiss tariff system is not regulated; patients mostly pay the costs themselves.

arbitrage_summary.text: Switzerland permits limited medical use of LSD through BAG per-patient exceptional permits requested by the treating physician; not a marketing authorisation.

legal_basis.value: Betäubungsmittelgesetz (BetmG, SR 812.121) Art. 8 Abs. 5 — BAG exceptional permits for limited medical use of prohibited narcotics

access_pathway_details.text: Under Art. 8(5) of the Narcotics Act (BetmG), the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) grants treating physicians case-by-case exceptional permits for limited medical use of LSD, MDMA or psilocybin in individual patients. Each permit covers one patient and one substance, is valid for one year and may be renewed; there is no entitlement to a permit.

eligibility_requirements.text: Serious illness where conventional treatments have been exhausted and relief can be expected. Post-traumatic stress disorder is among the most common primary indications. The physician's application includes the patient's written consent.

provider_requirements.text: Only the treating physician can apply to the BAG. Permit holders are usually specialists in psychiatry and psychotherapy; parts of the treatment can be delegated to other professionals.

oversight_notes.text: BAG per-patient exceptional permit system in place since 2014; about 1,800 permits (initial and renewals) were issued from 2014 to the end of 2024. It is an exception under narcotics law, not a marketing authorisation.

cost_notes.text: Billing within the Swiss tariff system is not regulated; patients mostly pay the costs themselves.

arbitrage_summary.text: Switzerland permits limited medical use of MDMA through BAG per-patient exceptional permits requested by the treating physician; not a marketing authorisation.
